description: VS Code extension that recursively finds nested .git folders and registers them with the built-in Git extension so they appear in Source Control automatically.

userStories.title: Scaffold VS Code extension project
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a compilable VS Code extension scaffold so that subsequent stories have a working foundation to build on.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json has correct VS Code extension fields: publisher, engines.vscode, main, activationEvents (onStartupFinished), contributes stub
tsconfig.json targets ES2020, module CommonJS, strict mode on
src/extension.ts exports activate() and deactivate() stubs that compile without errors
.gitignore covers node_modules, out/, *.vsix
.vscode/launch.json configured to run Extension Host for local debugging
npm run compile (tsc --noEmit) passes with zero errors

userStories.title: Implement recursive .git scanner
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a scanner module that recursively finds all .git directories under a given root, so the extension knows which repos to register.
acceptanceCriteria: src/scanner.ts exports findNestedGitRepos(rootDir: string, maxDepth: number): string[] — returns absolute paths of directories containing .git
Skips node_modules directories during traversal
Skips the root directory itself (only returns nested repos, not the root)
maxDepth 0 means unlimited recursion; positive number limits depth
Returns empty array when no nested .git found
npm run compile passes with zero errors

userStories.title: Register discovered repos with vscode.git API
userStories.description: As a developer, I want discovered repos registered with the built-in Git extension so they appear in the Source Control panel with full Git functionality.
acceptanceCriteria: src/registrar.ts exports registerRepositories(uris: vscode.Uri[]): Promise<void>
Uses vscode.extensions.getExtension('vscode.git')!.exports.getAPI(1) to get the Git API
Calls git.openRepository(uri) for each discovered repo path
Logs each registered repo path to the Output Channel (Nested Git Tracker)
Gracefully handles case where vscode.git extension is not available (logs warning, does not throw)
activate() in extension.ts calls scanner then registrar on startup
npm run compile passes with zero errors

userStories.title: Add maxDepth configuration setting
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to configure the scan depth via settings.json so I can limit scanning in large workspaces.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json contributes.configuration defines nestedGitTracker.maxDepth: type number, default 0, minimum 0, description explains 0 = unlimited
src/config.ts exports getMaxDepth(): number that reads the setting via vscode.workspace.getConfiguration
Invalid or missing value falls back to 0 (unlimited)
scanner.ts uses getMaxDepth() value
npm run compile passes with zero errors

userStories.title: Add manual rescan command
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to trigger a rescan from the Command Palette so I can pick up newly created repos without restarting VS Code.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json contributes.commands registers command nested-git-tracker.rescan with title 'Nested Git Tracker: Rescan Workspace'
Command handler re-runs scanner and registrar
Already-registered repo paths are skipped (no duplicate registration)
Output Channel logs count of newly found repos after rescan
npm run compile passes with zero errors
